lyrics:
[Intro: string stabs, finger snaps, bouncing bass, a voice calling]
Who's that? Who's that?
Come on over

[Verse 1: male rap, relaxed bounce, clear diction]
Pull up where the taco truck parks by the light
Kids doing wheelies in the last of the night
Miss Loretta on the stoop with the news and a fan
If you grew up on this block then you know who I am
Got the barber and the baker and the coach from the Y
Got an uncle with the stories that are forty per cent lie
We don't check your shoes and we don't check your plates
If you carry in the groceries, you're one of the greats

[Chorus: crowd call and response, claps on every beat]
Hey (hey), who's that?
One of us
From the east side?
One of us
With the bad knees?
One of us
Brought a plate?
Then you're one of us

[Verse 2: male rap, faster, playful]
New folks on the corner with the paint still wet
Wave when you see us, we ain't met you yet
Got a kid who needs a ride? Got a cat up a tree?
Got a cousin getting married? Bring the chairs, call me
We been here through the floods and the freeze and the fights
Through the landlords and the layoffs and the long summer nights
You can keep your gated driveway and your doorbell with a lens
We got eyes on every porch, and every porch is full of friends

[Chorus: crowd call and response, claps on every beat]
Hey (hey), who's that?
One of us
From the west side?
One of us
With the loud laugh?
One of us
Stayed to clean?
Then you're one of us

[Bridge: beat drops to snaps, one long held note, crowd joins]
O-o-o-o-o-o-one
Of us
Say it with your chest

[Final Chorus: full beat, whole block shouting, whistles]
Hey (hey), who's that?
One of us
Got a story?
One of us
Got nobody?
One of us
Come on in
Now you're one of us

[Outro: snaps and strings, children laughing, a grill hissing]
One of us
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 101 BPM, 4/4, C minor. A loose, bouncing West Coast party groove. Proud, funny and communal.

VOICE: A male rapper with a nimble, slightly high, animated voice who changes tone from line to line: teasing, warm, declamatory. A large crowd of all ages shouts the answers. In the bridge he stretches the first word of the title over a long, sliding held note and the crowd joins in.

INSTRUMENTS: Short, stabbing string hits in a repeating pattern. Finger snaps on the backbeat. A fat, bouncing 808 bass. A sparse kick. Handclaps from the crowd. A high synth whine in the chorus. Party sounds: whistles, laughter, a grill.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, string stabs, snaps and a call. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:48 Chorus 1, call and response. 1:07 Verse 2. 1:45 Chorus 2. 2:04 Bridge, the beat drops to snaps and the long held note. 2:23 Final chorus with the whole block. 2:52 The beat rides with ad-libs. 3:08 Outro, snaps and strings with street sounds, one last shout at 3:16.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2020s West Coast club rap: clean, sparse and bass-heavy, with the voice dry in the centre and the crowd wide around it.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The long, sliding held note at 2:04.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original draws a line to keep someone out. This one uses the same chant to count people in, including the new neighbours with wet paint. It is what the song became when crowds took it over.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Pride, welcome, unity.
